uncited: This method is an active view selection policy for robotic 3D reconstruction using Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF).
It selects the next best views by maximizing information gain, approximated via the mean entropy of a candidate view's uncertainty map.

It distinguishes itself from global greedy selection by enforcing spatial diversity through region clustering, preventing the selection of redundant, similar viewpoints that cause overfitting, while avoiding the slow coverage of single-view-per-iteration strategies.
- A set of candidate camera poses $\mathcal{C}$ distributed on a hemisphere surrounding the object.
- A current NeRF model $\mathcal{N}$ trained on an initial dataset $\mathcal{D}_{init}$.
- A target image resolution for uncertainty evaluation.
- A set of selected camera poses $\mathcal{S}$ to be captured in the current iteration.
- **View Space:** A hemisphere divided into 13 regions: 12 sections (clusters) and 1 middle circle (excluded from selection).
Each half is divided into 6 groups based on azimuthal angle $\phi$, resulting in 12 sections $R_1, \dots, R_{12}$.
- **Candidate Poses:** 30 poses per horizontal circle, 5 circles total, yielding 150 candidates.
- **Candidate Poses:** 150 total (30 per circle $\times$ 5 circles).
- **Initialization Images:** 6 for synthetic data, 15 for real-world data, sampled from the middle circle.
**Region Definition:** Divide the hemisphere into 12 sections for clustering.
Identify all candidate poses $c \in \mathcal{C}$ that fall within section $R_i$.
For each candidate pose $c$, render the scene using $\mathcal{N}$ to obtain the weight distribution $w$ for each pixel.
Compute the entropy $H(c, p)$ for each pixel $p$ in the rendered image.
Select the candidate pose $c^*_i$ with the highest mean entropy $\bar{H}(c)$ within section $R_i$.
Update the training dataset $\mathcal{D} \leftarrow \mathcal{D} \cup \mathcal{S}$.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of candidate poses (150) and the number of sections (12).
For each iteration, 12 candidates are evaluated.
Each evaluation requires rendering the scene and computing entropy for all pixels.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the NeRF model and the training dataset.
It achieves high-quality 3D meshes with fewer images than dense sampling.
- **Strengths:** Ensures diverse view selection, prevents overfitting, and accelerates coverage compared to single-view strategies.
Performance depends on the quality of the initial coarse reconstruction.
It builds on the concept of active robotic 3D reconstruction using NeRF, leveraging ray-based volumetric uncertainty estimation to guide view selection.
The approach addresses the challenge of efficiently selecting novel views to improve 3D reconstruction quality.
